sections.title: In everyday life
sections.bodyMarkdown:
### New requests arrive before a deadline

State what can be completed within the current deadline and which conditions must change to add more. Discussing specific trade-offs helps a shared decision more than a general statement that you cannot do it.

Identify whether the objection concerns evidence, wording or the conclusion. Correcting a factual mistake does not require abandoning every judgment. Keep your response focused on what you can support.

### You do not want to attend an event

Explain your availability briefly and clearly without inventing an excuse or offering endless justifications. If questions continue, you can repeat the decision rather than submit a new defence each time.

articleMarkdown:
# Seven of Wands: Name what you need to protect

Card: Seven of Wands  
Card marking: VII  
Minor Arcana · Wands  
Keywords: Position · Boundaries · Response

## At a glance

Upright: Stand your ground under pressure and explain what needs protecting

Reversed: You may be answering every challenge, or yielding because you cannot keep it up

Only one person is visible in the Seven of Wands, yet six wands reach towards that figure. First identify the pressure that genuinely requires a response rather than imagining an enemy behind every pole.

## A foothold above and six wands below

The figure stands with feet apart on green high ground, holding a wand diagonally across the body with both hands. A green tunic covers the slightly leaning body, and the face turns towards the lower right. The footwear differs: one side resembles a low shoe while the other covers the ankle. The difference is visible, but its cause is not explained.

Six wands extend upward from the lower edge; their holders are not shown. Rocky faces and uneven ground lie underfoot, with blue sky above. The difference in height creates tension: the figure has a foothold while facing pressure from below. The image does not show the outcome.

## Historical themes of courage and positional advantage

Waite links the card with courage and regards the higher position as an advantage. He also applies it to discussion, verbal contention, negotiation and competition. The confrontation can therefore be read in terms of positions and ideas, not only physical combat.

The old reversed entry mentions confusion, anxiety and a warning about indecision. Building on those themes, this article offers an original boundary exercise: decide what needs holding firm and what can change. Higher ground does not automatically confer moral rightness; firmness still needs reasons.

## Reading it upright

Upright, the card can ask you to take responsibility for an important position. When requests, objections or expectations keep coming, identify what you are protecting: time, quality, an agreement or basic respect. Specific boundaries are easier for other people to understand and easier to put into practice.

Standing firm does not require answering every remark. Address the most consequential objections first, provide evidence where it is needed and leave irrelevant judgments alone. Accepting reasonable changes can coexist with protecting core conditions. A strong position does not have to treat every concession as defeat.

## Reading it reversed

The reversal checks whether responding has exceeded your capacity. You might be explaining and defending constantly, spending time even on unimportant opinions. Or fear of being disliked may lead you to accept requests you cannot fulfil.

Rank the pressures and choose the one that most needs attention. If necessary, delay your response, ask for help or state the conditions you can accept. Where actual threats exist, safety and appropriate support matter more than proving courage. The card need not become an instruction to cope alone.

## In everyday life

### New requests arrive before a deadline

State what can be completed within the current deadline and which conditions must change to add more. Discussing specific trade-offs helps a shared decision more than a general statement that you cannot do it.

### A view you hold is challenged

Identify whether the objection concerns evidence, wording or the conclusion. Correcting a factual mistake does not require abandoning every judgment. Keep your response focused on what you can support.

### You do not want to attend an event

Explain your availability briefly and clearly without inventing an excuse or offering endless justifications. If questions continue, you can repeat the decision rather than submit a new defence each time.

## A short exercise

Complete: “I am willing to…, but I cannot currently…; to continue, we would need….” Check whether each blank describes a specific action. Remove anything added to please someone that you cannot actually deliver.

## Common misreadings

The Seven of Wands does not prove that a group is against you, or that the person who holds out longest is right. It offers practice in reasoned firmness while leaving room to check facts, change methods and seek support.

## Artwork and English sources

- [Pamela Colman Smith, Seven of Wands, RWS Pam-A / TaionWC](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Wands07.jpg)
- [A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot, Part III §2, Seven of Wands (1911-labelled English transcription)](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktwa07.htm)

Sources checked: 2026-10-07. This article translates the original Chinese learning text. The English source is a transcription labelled 1911; the image file page describes a 1910 Pam-A card. Historical context and contemporary exercises are identified separately.

sourceRecord.title: 权杖七 说清你要守住什么
sourceRecord.uprightQuickTake: 有压力也要站稳，把需要守住的事说清楚
sourceRecord.reversedQuickTake: 忙着应付所有质疑，或撑不住想让步
sourceRecord.hook: 权杖七里能看见的人只有一个，伸向他的木杖却有六根。读这张牌，先辨认真正需要回应的压力，别急着把每根杖都想成一个敌人。
imageReading: 人物站在绿色高地上，两脚分开，双手将一根木杖斜横在身前。他穿着绿色短衣，身体微微倾斜，脸朝向画面右下方。脚上的穿着不完全相同：一边像低鞋，另一边包到脚踝以上。这个差异可见，形成原因却没有被说明。
六根木杖从画面下缘向上伸来，握杖的人没有出现在画中。脚下有岩石切面与起伏地形，上方是一片蓝天。位置高低构成明显张力：人物有立足点，也承受来自下方的压力；牌图并没有画出最终结果。
tradition: Waite 将此牌联系到勇气，并把高处的位置视为优势。他也把它用于讨论、言语交锋、谈判与竞争。因此，画面的对抗可以发展到立场与意见层面，不必只读成身体上的战斗。
旧书逆位谈到困惑、焦虑以及对犹豫的提醒。本篇在此基础上提出原创的边界练习：决定什么需要坚持、什么可以调整。高处并不自动代表道德正确，坚定也需要有理由。
uprightMeaning: 正位可以提醒你对一个重要立场负责。当新增要求、反对意见或外界期待接连出现，先确认自己要保护的是时间、质量、约定，还是基本的尊重。边界越具体，越容易让别人理解，也越容易实际执行。
站稳不等于回应每一句话。你可以先处理影响最大的意见，对需要证据的部分补充说明，对无关评价暂不投入。允许合理修改，与守住核心条件可以同时发生；真正有力的立场通常不需要把所有让步都当成失败。
reversedMeaning: 逆位可用来检查应对是否超出了余力。一种情况是不断解释、不断防守，连不重要的意见也占走大量时间；另一种是因为害怕不被喜欢，答应了自己无法履行的要求。
先给压力排序，选择最需要处理的一件。必要时延后回应、请人协助，或清楚说明可接受的条件。若现实中存在威胁，安全与适当支持比证明自己勇敢更重要；不必借牌要求自己独自硬撑。

situations.title: 期限前又加了新要求
situations.text: 明确说明现有期限内能完成什么，增加内容需要调整哪项条件。讨论具体取舍，比笼统表示“我做不到”更有利于共同决定。

situations.title: 一个观点受到质疑
situations.text: 先分辨对方是在质疑证据、表达方式还是结论。愿意修正事实错误，并不意味着要放弃所有判断；把回应集中在有依据的部分。

situations.title: 不想参加某次活动
situations.text: 用简短而清楚的话表达安排，不必编造理由或无限解释。如果对方继续追问，可以重复自己的决定，而不是不断提交新的辩护。

sourceRecord.practice: 补完这句话：“我愿意配合……，但目前不能……；如果要继续，需要……。”检查三个空格能否描述具体行为。然后删去其中为了讨好别人而加入、自己无法兑现的部分。
sourceRecord.commonMisread: 权杖七不证明你被集体针对，也不说明坚持得最久的人就是对的。它让你练习有依据的坚定，同时保留核对事实、改变方法与寻求支持的余地。
sourceRecord.sourceClaim: Waite 的勇气、位置优势、讨论与谈判，及逆位犹豫提醒；六根杖的持有者不在画中。边界和压力排序为原创现代应用。
